title: Symmetry-Based Microscopic Theory of the Unconventional Pairing Mechanism in La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$
abstract: Recent experiments report high-temperature superconductivity in the hybrid nickelate $\mathrm{La}_5\mathrm{Ni}_3\mathrm{O}_{11}$, which is composed of alternating stacks of bilayer $\mathrm{La}_3\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ and monolayer $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{NiO}_4$. However, the superconducting transition temperature $T_c \approx 64~\mathrm{K}$ for $\mathrm{La}_5\mathrm{Ni}_3\mathrm{O}_{11}$ is remarkably lower than the $80~\mathrm{K}$ observed for pressurized $\mathrm{La}_3\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_7$. Thus, an unified microscopic theory is required to address the difference in the pairing mechanisms between these systems. Here, we develop a phenomenological symmetry-based approach to systematically analyze the low-energy physics in $\mathrm{La}_5\mathrm{Ni}_3\mathrm{O}_{11}$, which is obtained by a charge self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory method. We show that the superconductivity in $\mathrm{La}_5\mathrm{Ni}_3\mathrm{O}_{11}$ exhibits a two-gap nature, consisting of a leading interlayer pairing between the $d_{z^2}$ orbitals and a subleading intralayer pairing between the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals. The reduction of $T_c$ can be attributed to the diminished contribution of the interlayer pairing, as reflected by the hopping parameter ratio $|t_{\perp}^z/t_{\parallel}^{x}|$. Base on this unified picture, we discuss the possible pairing mechanism and the role of $γ$ pocket for the superconductivity in the bilayer NiO$_2$ planes of nickelate superconductors.
summary: This work develops a symmetry-based microscopic theory to explain superconductivity in nickelates. It finds that La5Ni3O11 exhibits a two-gap superconducting state, attributing the lower $T_c$ compared to related materials to changes in orbital hopping ratios. The methodology combines advanced electronic structure calculations with rigorous group-theoretical analysis of pairing symmetries.
main_problem: To develop a unified microscopic theory explaining the difference in superconducting pairing mechanisms between nickelate superconductors like La5Ni3O11 and pressurized La3Ni2O7.
main_result: The superconductivity in La5Ni3O11 is characterized by a two-gap nature, involving leading interlayer pairing ($d_{z^2}$) and subleading intralayer pairing ($d_{x^2-y^2}$), with the reduction of Tc attributed to the hopping parameter ratio $|t_{\perp}^z/t_{\parallel}^{x}|$.
method: The study employs a symmetry-based approach combined with advanced many-body techniques, including DFT+DMFT and analysis via the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is based on nickelate superconductors (e.g., La5Ni3O11), modeled using an effective quasiparticle Hamiltonian derived from strong correlation physics involving Ni-$e_g$ orbitals.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), superconducting gap structure ($\Delta_{sz^2}$ vs $\Delta_{sx^2+y^2}$), and the hopping parameter ratio $|t_{\perp}^z/t_{\parallel}^{x}|$.
important_parameters: $T_c \approx 64$ K for La5Ni3O11; $T_c = 80$ K for pressurized La3Ni2O7.
main_assumptions: The low-energy physics is dominated by Ni-$e_g$ orbitals, and the pairing mechanism can be analyzed using symmetry constraints on the gap function.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops a theoretical framework starting from DFT+DMFT calculations to analyze the low-energy physics, determining the superconducting state via minimizing the free energy functional derived from the BdG Hamiltonian.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the use of symmetry constraints and mean-field approaches to determine pairing instabilities is relevant for understanding emergent order parameters in complex quantum systems.
